headline: Resolution to end the 2004 national emergency behind U.S. sanctions on Syria was voted down in the House.
what_it_does: This resolution would have ended a national emergency that President George W. Bush declared on May 11, 2004, regarding Syria. That emergency is the legal basis for blocking the property of certain people and limiting the export of certain goods to Syria. It was declared in response to Syria supporting terrorist activity in Iraq, among other actions. The House voted it down on July 18, 2023.

who_it_affects.group: People and entities whose property is blocked under the Syria emergency
who_it_affects.how: They could have lost the legal basis for having their property in the U.S. frozen.
Limits on exporting certain goods to Syria that rely on this emergency could have ended.
It could have faced fewer U.S. sanctions tied to this emergency.
